artifacts.notes: Retained because the seventh prefatory question on Genesis 15 is the earliest identified statement of the difficulty that the star-promise of Genesis 15:5 precedes the chapter's own sunset, and because it is the load-bearing witness for a publication's central historical finding. Abbreviations and Hebrew numerals are left exactly as the transcriptions give them; the citation of the Talmud in question 7 as Shabbat 157 corresponds to the passage cited by modern foliation as Shabbat 156a.
artifacts.rights_basis: Three short passages of a Hebrew commentary first printed in the sixteenth century, from an 1862 printing that is out of copyright by age. The header block is Triptych editorial description; Triptych claims no exclusive right in the source wording.

work.author: Isaac ben Judah Abarbanel
work.description: Don Isaac Abarbanel's commentary on the Pentateuch, composed after his expulsion from Spain in 1492 and first printed in the sixteenth century. Its distinctive method is to preface each unit with a numbered list of difficulties and then to expound the verses so that the difficulties are resolved; the question lists are therefore a primary record of what a fifteenth-century reader found hard in a passage. A locus is BookToken.chapter or BookToken.chapter.verse; prefatory questions are cited by chapter with the question number stated in prose.
work.title: Perush al ha-Torah
